new_candidates.body:
## Environment

- gz-transport 13.6.0 (`libgz-transport13 13.6.0-1~noble`, Python bindings `python3-gz-transport13`), Ubuntu 24.04
- Default discovery (UDP multicast), all processes on one host
- Default `net.core.rmem_default = net.core.rmem_max = 212992`

## Description

When a process advertises many topics at once, some subscriptions in other processes never receive any message, even though the topics are published continuously. They stay silent until the subscriber unsubscribes and subscribes again. Waiting doesn't help (we waited minutes).

We found this in Gazebo Harmonic: spawning models with sensors into a running gz-sim server, while other processes (PX4 SITL) subscribed to the new sensor topics. The reproducer below needs only gz-transport.

## Reproducer

The script starts S subscriber processes. Each subscribes to N topics that are not advertised yet. Then one publisher process advertises all N topics at once and publishes each at 10 Hz. After 25 s every subscriber reports the topics that never delivered a message.

Scripts: https://gist.github.com/spurnvoj/6d4fee0f03a7b75f2da72be6932ae486 (`bash run_repro.sh`, or `N=100 S=2 bash run_repro.sh`)

Results on one machine (each run started fresh):

| rmem_default | topics | subscriber processes | UDP drops on port 10317 (all sockets) | silent subscriptions per subscriber |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 212992 (default) | 300 | 4 | 13881 | 79 / 300 |
| 212992 (default) | 300 | 4 | 41298 | 50 / 300 |
| 212992 (default) | 100 | 2 | 1537 | 26 / 100 |
| 212992 (default) | 50 | 1 | 17 | 0 / 50 |
| 8388608 | 300 | 4 | 0 | 0 / 300 |

All subscriber processes were silent on **exactly the same** topics.

## Cause, as far as we can tell from the source

1. **The publisher only sends to remote subscribers it has registered.** It checks `remoteSubscribers.HasTopic()` ([NodeShared.cc#L550](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-transport/blob/gz-transport13_13.6.0/src/NodeShared.cc#L550), [Node.cc#L499](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-transport/blob/gz-transport13_13.6.0/src/Node.cc#L499)).
2. **Only `OnNewRegistration` fills that table**, when the subscriber's `NEW_CONNECTION` arrives ([NodeShared.cc#L1287](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-transport/blob/gz-transport13_13.6.0/src/NodeShared.cc#L1287)).
3. **`NEW_CONNECTION` is sent exactly once.** `OnNewConnection` sends it as a single UDP multicast datagram via `Discovery::Register()` ([NodeShared.cc#L1179](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-transport/blob/gz-transport13_13.6.0/src/NodeShared.cc#L1179), [Discovery.hh#L406](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-transport/blob/gz-transport13_13.6.0/include/gz/transport/Discovery.hh#L406)).
   - It is not acknowledged and never retried.
   - `ENOBUFS` on send is ignored ([Discovery.hh#L1369](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-transport/blob/gz-transport13_13.6.0/include/gz/transport/Discovery.hh#L1369)).
   - Heartbeat re-advertisements do not trigger `OnNewConnection` again for a known publisher ([Discovery.hh#L1044-L1050](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-transport/blob/gz-transport13_13.6.0/include/gz/transport/Discovery.hh#L1044-L1050)).
4. **The discovery sockets keep the system default receive buffer.** Only `SO_REUSEADDR`/`SO_REUSEPORT` are set, no `SO_RCVBUF` ([Discovery.hh#L194-L215](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-transport/blob/gz-transport13_13.6.0/include/gz/transport/Discovery.hh#L194-L215)).

When many topics are advertised at once, the burst of ADVERTISE/NEW_CONNECTION traffic overflows the default 208 KB receive buffer and datagrams are dropped (see the drop counters above). A topic whose `NEW_CONNECTION`s were all lost is never sent, permanently.

This also explains the other observations (the last two are from the gz-sim setup, not from the reproducer):
- **Every subscriber is silent on the same topics,** because the gate is per topic: one successful registration makes the publisher send to all subscribers of that topic.
- **Re-subscribing heals it,** because it sends a fresh `NEW_CONNECTION`.
- **`gz topic -i` still lists the silent subscribers,** because that list comes from the subscribers' own `SUBSCRIBERS_REP`.

## Possible fixes

- **Re-send `NEW_CONNECTION`** while the publisher is known (e.g. with the heartbeat, or until acknowledged), so a lost datagram heals itself. `OnNewRegistration` already tolerates duplicates.
- **Request a larger `SO_RCVBUF`** on the discovery sockets, possibly configurable through an environment variable.
- **Log a warning** on `ENOBUFS` instead of ignoring it.

The workaround for now is raising `net.core.rmem_default` (and `net.core.rmem_max`), e.g. to 8 MB.
new_candidates.title: Subscriptions stay silent forever when the one-shot NEW_CONNECTION discovery datagram is dropped

new_candidates.body:
[camera_failure.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33377722/camera_failure.log)
[camera_pose_call.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33377723/camera_pose_call.txt)
[fabric_frame_view.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33377725/fabric_frame_view.py)
[fabric_frame_view_local.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33377724/fabric_frame_view_local.patch)

### Describe the bug

After several hours of repeated camera pose updates and rendering, `Camera.set_world_poses()` fails because the writable Fabric selection no longer exports a valid `omni:fabric:worldMatrix` array descriptor. The selection still matches all 256 camera prims. Calling `PrepareForReuse()` and rebuilding the selection with `SelectPrims()` do not restore the descriptor, so the simulation stops.

We cannot yet tell whether the underlying Fabric attribute disappears, its array-interface export fails, or our use of the API is incorrect. The attached code shows the exact view implementation and camera call.

### Steps to reproduce

We do not have a deterministic short reproducer. The failure occurred with `use_fabric=True`, 256 cameras, an RTX renderer, and a persistent `FabricFrameView`. The application repeatedly calls `Camera.set_world_poses()` to capture images from different camera poses, with occasional USD scene-payload changes. After approximately eight hours, a pose update failed. No payload change was in progress at that call. The attachment contains `camera_pose_call.txt`, the current `fabric_frame_view.py`, its local patch, and the relevant console log.

```text
2026-10-13T02:09:28Z [Warning] FabricFrameView: rebuilt _sel_rw after incomplete array interface (missing ['omni:fabric:worldMatrix'])
  File ".../camera.py", line 384, in set_world_poses
    writer.set_poses(pos_wp, ori_wp, idx_wp)
  File ".../fabric_frame_view.py", line 1011, in set_poses
    view._get_world_ifa()
  File ".../fabric_frame_view.py", line 649, in _selection_interface
    raise RuntimeError(...)
RuntimeError: FabricFrameView: _sel_rw array interface still missing ['omni:fabric:worldMatrix'] after rebuild
```

### System Info

- Isaac Lab checkout: `release/3.0.0-beta2`, commit `99f1423e5d4a26216c0eedeb2aa78099a8c3a7d1`, with the attached local `fabric_frame_view.py` patch
- Isaac Sim: `6.0.1-rc.7+release.42383.32955d8d.gl`; Kit: `110.1.2+production.326809.f9bf0dda.gl`
- Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS; Python 3.12.13
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090; driver 580.173.02
- PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128; CUDA 12.8; Warp 1.13.0

### Additional context

The view calls `PrepareForReuse()`, checks that the selection count is still 256, and inspects `selection.__fabric_arrays_interface__["attribs"]`. When the matrix descriptor is absent or invalid, it synchronizes the device and creates a new selection requiring `Matrix4d` read/write access. The new selection also lacks a valid `worldMatrix` descriptor. We did not capture the raw interface or each prim's attribute state at the first failure.

The last logged GPU-memory samples were steady at about 22.4 GiB used and 9.0 GiB free. The console shows no OOM or Vulkan allocation error near the failure. Those samples cannot exclude a transient event between measurements.

Is this `SelectPrims()`/`PrepareForReuse()` usage supported for persistent writable camera transforms? Is there a recommended way to diagnose and recover a missing `worldMatrix` export without restarting the simulation?

I searched IsaacLab issues for this exact error and found no match. [#6394](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/issues/6394) also concerns Fabric cameras, but describes stale images after reset rather than a missing writable array descriptor.

### Checklist

- [x] I checked for a similar issue in the repo.
- [ ] I have not yet established whether the underlying fault is in Isaac Lab, Isaac Sim/USDRT, or the attached local view implementation.

new_candidates.body:
### Description

While running a headless simulation that uses **`omni.anim.behavior.core`** (animated digital humans) on top of the default environment ground plane, the console is **continuously spammed** with:

```
[Warning] [omni.meshraycast.plugin] Unable to create mesh representation for prim /World/GroundPlane/GroundPlane/CollisionPlane, raycast will skip it.
```

The warning is emitted repeatedly during playback (the behavior/anim system rebuilds/refreshes its mesh-raycast BVH while the character is active), producing very noisy logs.

### Environment

- Isaac Sim: **6.1.0-rc.26** (build `6.1.0-rc.26+main.0.7c206f75.local`, Kit 110)
- App: `isaacsim.exp.full.kit` with `--no-window` (headless)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, NVIDIA vGPU
- Relevant extensions:
  - `omni.kit.mesh.raycast-110.0.0`
  - `omni.anim.behavior.core-110.3.5`
  - `omni.anim.navigation.core-*`, `omni.anim.graph.core-*`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Isaac Sim (full app) headless.
2. Load the default environment ground: `/Isaac/Environments/Grid/default_environment.usd`, referenced at `/World/GroundPlane` (this produces the nested prim `/World/GroundPlane/GroundPlane/CollisionPlane`).
3. Add a character driven by `omni.anim.behavior.core` (e.g. a digital human with a BehaviorAgentAPI + motion library) and play the timeline / run the sim loop.
4. Observe the console.

### Expected behavior

Either no warning, or the warning is emitted at most once (the ground plane is a known non-mesh primitive that the mesh raycast intentionally cannot support).

### Actual behavior

```
[Warning] [omni.meshraycast.plugin] Unable to create mesh representation for prim /World/GroundPlane/GroundPlane/CollisionPlane, raycast will skip it.
```

…repeated continuously during playback (log spam).

### Root-cause analysis

- The message comes from the native plugin `omni.meshraycast.plugin` shipped in extension **`omni.kit.mesh.raycast`** (`bin/libomni.kit.mesh.raycast.plugin.so`). That plugin builds a BVH of **PhysX triangle meshes** cooked from USD `Mesh` geometry (`cookTriMesh` / `PxTriangleMesh`) and performs standalone PhysX scene-query raycasts.
- The extension is auto-started in this setup **because of `omni.anim.behavior.core`**. Confirmed in the Kit log:

  ```
  [ext: omni.kit.mesh.raycast-110.0.0] ... About to startup: ... Triggered by: isaacsim.exp.full-6.0.1, omni.anim.behavior.core-*
  ```

- The offending prim is an **infinite `UsdGeom.Plane`** (the `CollisionPlane` under the default environment's `GroundPlane`). A `UsdGeom.Plane` has **no triangle/vertex data**, so no triangle-mesh representation can be cooked for it. Hence the warning on every BVH (re)build.

### Impact

- **Functional:** none observed. PhysX rigid-body/plane collision is handled natively by PhysX and is unaffected; the ground collision still works. The mesh-raycast path simply skips the plane.
- **Log noise:** severe — the warning is repeated continuously, drowning out useful output and making logs/CI hard to read.

### Suggested fix (one of)

1. Skip infinite `Plane` prims **silently** (debug-level log) in `omni.kit.mesh.raycast` instead of warning on every BVH build.
2. Emit the warning **once per prim** (deduplicate), not once per BVH rebuild.
3. If a mesh representation for the ground is actually required by `omni.anim.behavior.core`, document / provide a supported way to use a finite mesh or cuboid ground so the BVH has triangles to build.

### Additional notes

- Replacing the default environment's infinite-plane ground with a finite mesh/cuboid ground eliminates the warning, but that is a workaround, not a fix — the default environment ships with a `Plane`-based ground out of the box.
